text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 12: At lead-day 14, B0 is worse than climatology and a random-day lag gains too'
text.tspan: Figure 12: At lead-day 14, B0 is worse than climatology and a random-day

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Top: each arm's mean absolute error minus B0's at the same lead-day, in percentage points of capacity; below zero beats B0. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Bottom: the mean absolute error of B0, L1, and climatology, in percentage points of capacity; smaller is better. A random-day lag (N2) gains at the longest lead too, so part of the lag arms' long-lead gain is not specific to recent days.'

text.aria-label: Title text 'Lead-day is the number of days between the weather forecast run and the target day. The weather forecast is the mean of the ensemble (ENS) from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). Fits are per plant, at the primary setting (depth 6, learning rate 0.05, 500 rounds, and row subsampling 0.8). 0*: lead-day 0 is not usable for its early hours in a live service. All rows are exploratory. Arms. B0: the baseline with no lag. L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). W7: the minimum, maximum, and mean of the same hour over the last 7 whole days. Q30: the 30-day 90th percentile and median of the same hour. T1: days since the record began. Month- block folds interleave, so trees can interpolate a scored month's level from months on both sides; its gain is what interpolation buys, never drift a live forecast could use. N2: a random day from months not being scored (a null control). climatology: the median power of the plant's calendar month and hour, from months outside the scored block, with no fit.'
text.tspan: Lead-day is the number of days between the weather forecast run and the target day. The weather forecast is the mean of the
ensemble (ENS) from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). Fits are per plant, at the primary
setting (depth 6, learning rate 0.05, 500 rounds, and row subsampling 0.8).
0*: lead-day 0 is not usable for its early hours in a live service.
Arms. B0: the baseline with no lag. L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was
issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). W7: the minimum, maximum, and mean of the same hour over
the last 7 whole days. Q30: the 30-day 90th percentile and median of the same hour. T1: days since the record began. Month-
block folds interleave, so trees can interpolate a scored month's level from months on both sides; its gain is what
interpolation buys, never drift a live forecast could use. N2: a random day from months not being scored (a null control).
climatology: the median power of the plant's calendar month and hour, from months outside the scored block, with no fit.
